items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-24
items.q: And I have worked with Charlie Parker and I have recorded Charlie Parker

ctx.x: No, what happened with Charlie Parker is that, to a certain extent, he became a romantic hero of the beat generation. Oh, yes. Ferlinghetti, all the New York beat things. Now, the question as to why he did is somehow they read into his music a lot of protest themes. And, of course, you can take any musician's thing and read anything you wanted to it. But it's interesting that he became a kind of a basis for a romantic legend the same way Bix did. That is, in New York and Subway Walls, you'd have Bird Lives.

That's true. But as far as music is concerned, I mean, I can't understand the response of people to Mick Jagger or Alice Cooper and so on, because it is completely aesthetically meaningless to me. And I have worked with Charlie Parker and I have recorded Charlie Parker, and I have paid close and, I think, objective attention, or at least objective as much as I could be. And I found it certainly unexceptional.
It seems, Al, that socially and politically, we haven't really talked about your political views yet, but you say that you're a revolutionary socialist.

items.title: Al Rose Interview, 1976-02-19
items.q: And I considered him to be a pleasant personality.

ctx.x: Who was the most smelty organ player in the world. And there was no way by listening to Fats Waller's music that you were going to say that he was influenced by that organ.

Well, what I am saying is that if you listen to Rudy Valli, and especially to Dick Stabile on records, and if you listen to them... You're going to hear all those fast changes that Parker makes? You're going to hear all those things that Parker makes. I don't believe it. Well, try it and see. I don't believe that. I recommend that you try it and see, because it'll be illuminating for you to do that. And I considered that Charlie Parker was very pleasant. He had a tendency to be narcissistic. He was friendly but…
I hear a lot of protest in Charlie Parker.
